senses.gloss: m. (præpositus, πραιπόσιτος) præpositus, a title of several imperial officers, esp. (= magister militum) chief of the army.
units: <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 1">Num. R. s. 1</cite>, end <he>אומר פ׳ לך מנה וכ׳</he> (not <he>סוטוט …</he>) he says to the præpositus, go and count all legions except &c.
<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 15:17">Ex. R. s. 15</cite> <he>נכנס פרוסביטוס וכ׳</he> (corr. acc.) the præpositus with his suite went in &c.

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 7">Num. R. s. 7</cite> <he>בו״ד יש לו פריפיסיטין וכ׳</he> (read: <he>פְּרִיפּוֹ׳</he>) a human king has præpositi (to muster the army), and so the Lord has (ref. to <cite ref="Numbers 1:2">Num. I, 2</cite>). Y’lamd. to Num. X, 1, quot. in Ar. <he>והיו הפ׳ באין תחלה וכ׳</he> the præpositi came first (to the headquarters), and then the legions.
